papers.title: Galileo’s Encounter with 243 Ida: An Overview of the Imaging Experiment
papers.examined: Relevant narrative plus visually inspected complete Table I (page 3), Table IIA (pages 5–7), Table III (page 14). This is not a close reading of every page.
papers.finding: Table III explicitly gives east longitudes: Acmon -39/138, Celmis -46/220 degrees. Table IIA values match Ida geometry, not a Dactyl body-frame solution. Table I gives Dactyl spin >8 hours, rather than a unique pole/phase.

papers.title: Discovery of a satellite of the asteroid 243 Ida and its physical properties
papers.examined: Author preprint text; illustrations were not available in this PostScript copy.
papers.finding: Published ellipsoid dimensions, long axis within about 15 degrees of Ida and spin period greater than about 8 hours constrain orientation without specifying a measured full body frame.

papers.title: Ida and Dactyl: Spectral Reflectance and Color Variations
papers.examined: All eleven pages, figures and the filter table.
papers.finding: Dactyl is represented by disk-averaged spectra; mapped figures are Ida. No Dactyl observation-specific body frame or distributed surface controls are provided.

papers.title: Photogrammetric Evaluation of Galileo SSI Ida Images: Preliminary Results
papers.examined: Extracted text of both pages, including the methods, Ida results and Ida satellite paragraph; no numerical controls were transcribed from figures.
papers.finding: The 96-point network and more than 5000 matched points are on Ida. The Dactyl paragraph proposes deriving an ephemeris; it does not provide Dactyl surface controls or a body-frame camera.

additionalKernels.examined: File introduction/body inventory and full-file searches for Dactyl and 2431011.
additionalKernels.finding: No Dactyl record in this generic PCK; this is a file-specific exclusion, not an archive-wide claim.
